questions.question: Comment on the freezing point and boiling point of milk.
questions.solution_html:
• Comment onthe freezingpoint andboilingpoint ofmilk.
  • Freezingpoint ofmilk
  •  The normal freezingpoint ofmilkis approximately\(-0.54^\circ C\).
  •  It is lower than that of pure water because milk contains dissolved substances such as
  • lactose andmineral salts.
  •  The freezingpoint is relativelyconstant innormal milk.
  •  Addition of water raises the freezing point towards \(0^\circ C\), making freezing-point
  • measurement useful fordetectingpossible adulterationwithwater.
  • Boilingpoint ofmilk
  •  Milk boils at a temperature slightly above that of pure water at the same atmospheric
  • pressure.
  •  At normal atmospheric pressure, its boiling point is approximately \(100.1–100.2^\circ
  • C\).
  •  Dissolvedsolids inmilkcause this slight elevationinboilingpoint.
  •  The boiling point decreases at lower atmospheric pressure and increases at higher
  • pressure.
  • Packagingandstorage: The cheese is packedhygienicallyandstoredunderrefrigeration.
  • Quality of raw milk: Initial microbial load, acidity, adulteration and the health of the milch
  • animals influence the qualityofmilkduringtransportation.

questions.question: Describe the carbohydrate and mineral value of milk.
questions.solution_html:
• Carbohydrate value
  •  Lactose is the principal carbohydrate inmilk.
  •  It is generallypresent at about 4.5–5.0%.
  •  Lactose provides energyandcontributes tothe mildsweetness ofmilk.
  •  It promotes calcium absorption and serves as a substrate for lactic acid bacteria during
  • fermentation.
  •  Fermentation of lactose produces lactic acid, which is important in the manufacture of
  • curd,yoghurt andcheese.
  • Mineral value
  •  Milk is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, which are essential for the
  • development andmaintenance ofbones andteeth.
  •  Potassium helps maintainfluidbalance andsupports normal muscle andnerve function.
  •  Sodium andchloride helpmaintainelectrolyte balance.
  •  Magnesium supports normal enzyme andmuscle functions.
  •  Milkalsocontains small amounts oftrace minerals,includingzinc,ironandcopper.
  • Availability of trained personnel: Properly trained milk handlers and drivers help maintain
  • hygiene,temperature control andaccurate records.
  • Measures toimprove transportation
  •  Cool milkpromptlyaftermilking.
  •  Use clean,food-grade milkcans andproperlysanitizedtankers.
  •  Maintainthe coldchainandminimize transportationdelays.
  •  Establishefficient collectioncentres andbulkmilkcoolingfacilities.
  •  Conduct regularqualitytestingat collectionandreceptionpoints.
  • Conclusion: Efficient transportation requires proper cooling, hygienic handling, suitable
  • infrastructure and effective milk collection systems. These measures help preserve milk quality
  • from the farm tothe dairyplant.

questions.question: Comment on the freezing point and boiling point of milk.
questions.solution_html:
• Comment onthe freezingpoint andboilingpoint ofmilk.
  • Freezingpoint ofmilk
  •  The normal freezingpoint ofmilkis approximately\(-0.54^\circ C\).
  •  It is lower than that of pure water because milk contains dissolved substances such as
  • lactose andmineral salts.
  •  The freezingpoint is relativelyconstant innormal milk.
  •  Addition of water raises the freezing point towards \(0^\circ C\), making freezing-point
  • measurement useful fordetectingpossible adulterationwithwater.
  • Boilingpoint ofmilk
  •  Milk boils at a temperature slightly above that of pure water at the same atmospheric
  • pressure.
  •  At normal atmospheric pressure, its boiling point is approximately \(100.1–100.2^\circ
  • C\).
  •  Dissolvedsolids inmilkcause this slight elevationinboilingpoint.
  •  The boiling point decreases at lower atmospheric pressure and increases at higher
  • pressure.
  • Packagingandstorage: The cheese is packedhygienicallyandstoredunderrefrigeration.
  • Quality of raw milk: Initial microbial load, acidity, adulteration and the health of the milch
  • animals influence the qualityofmilkduringtransportation.

questions.question: Describe the carbohydrate and mineral value of milk.
questions.solution_html:
• Carbohydrate value
  •  Lactose is the principal carbohydrate inmilk.
  •  It is generallypresent at about 4.5–5.0%.
  •  Lactose provides energyandcontributes tothe mildsweetness ofmilk.
  •  It promotes calcium absorption and serves as a substrate for lactic acid bacteria during
  • fermentation.
  •  Fermentation of lactose produces lactic acid, which is important in the manufacture of
  • curd,yoghurt andcheese.
  • Mineral value
  •  Milk is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, which are essential for the
  • development andmaintenance ofbones andteeth.
  •  Potassium helps maintainfluidbalance andsupports normal muscle andnerve function.
  •  Sodium andchloride helpmaintainelectrolyte balance.
  •  Magnesium supports normal enzyme andmuscle functions.
  •  Milkalsocontains small amounts oftrace minerals,includingzinc,ironandcopper.
  • Availability of trained personnel: Properly trained milk handlers and drivers help maintain
  • hygiene,temperature control andaccurate records.
  • Measures toimprove transportation
  •  Cool milkpromptlyaftermilking.
  •  Use clean,food-grade milkcans andproperlysanitizedtankers.
  •  Maintainthe coldchainandminimize transportationdelays.
  •  Establishefficient collectioncentres andbulkmilkcoolingfacilities.
  •  Conduct regularqualitytestingat collectionandreceptionpoints.
  • Conclusion: Efficient transportation requires proper cooling, hygienic handling, suitable
  • infrastructure and effective milk collection systems. These measures help preserve milk quality
  • from the farm tothe dairyplant.
